_comment: Models used by the /fenster-new-home-page/ experiment. Copied from C:\Users\zacpl\Desktop\windowcad-spins\models — originals untouched. Every entry below is a DISTINCT mesh: all 13 files verified unique by MD5 on 2026-08-21, so nothing here presents the same geometry as two different products. Source of truth for what genuinely varies is the fenstertrade manifest and 3d.md; the short version is that SIZE is only a real axis for bifolds, which is why no size variants appear here at all — this page shows one model per product, never a fake range.
_source: WindowCAD (windowsoftware.co.uk) retail configurator, exported as real scene geometry. WindowSoftware IP — local experiment only, not for redistribution. See 3d.md §11.
_materials: No textures in any file (images=0). A finish is baseColorFactor + metalness/roughness only, so colour is a RUNTIME change, not a file. Classification rule from 3d.md: translucent (alphaMode BLEND or alpha<1) is glass; opaque AND neutral (r≈g≈b) is frame or hardware.
_animation: The seven 'animated' entries each carry one baked clip named 'open-close', 5.00s, running shut -> open -> shut. This page scrubs the FIRST HALF only against scroll, so scrolling physically opens the product.

_not_included.upvc-doors.glb: 22,807 tris / 2.1 MB for a product the doors phase already covers with composite and aluminium. Weight without a distinct visual beat.
_not_included.composite-doors.glb: Byte-identical geometry to composite-front-door.glb, which is the animated version. Using both would be the exact duplicate-as-variety trap.
_not_included.aluminium-bifold-doors.glb: Static twin of aluminium-bifold-door.glb. Same reason.
_not_included.aluminium-sliding-patio-doors.glb: Static twin of the animated slider.
